2 · Paste the post copy

750 camera feeds is the ceiling Anchorage funded for its police crime center.

It opened last September with about 15 cameras and one employee.

Seven days left. Three members introduced surveillance rules on August 18th. On September 1st they share a table with a roughly $600,000 equipment contract.

The AI in the center today reads plates. The chief says police don't use facial recognition. The rule would require Assembly approval before AI powered tracking or identification is added.

Inside, the launch state, the four proposed rules and the retention clocks that are practice and not code.

A rule is cheap to write while the machine is small. If the money passes and the rules don't, what should happen to the feeds nobody has switched on?

#AnchorageAssembly #PolicingTech #AKPolitics

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

engine		DECLARED ARTWORK NOW HAS TO REACH THE SLIDE. A slide names the drawn features that carry meaning, window.__akMotifs = [{what, rect:[x,y,w,h]}] in design px; render.py reads that rect back out of the canvas the motif was drawn on and takes an elementsFromPoint census of what stands on it, and qa.py samples the same rect out of the composited PNG. FAILS when 15 percent or less of the rect is clear of opaque DOM, when the rect is one flat colour in the render, or when under 25 percent of the ink the canvas holds survives to the page. Opt-in like every other declaration contract, so a slide that declares nothing is not judged, and every FAIL is the slide contradicting itself. Two calibration facts are in the code: the ink statistic is the mean of the top 1 percent of dE from the region's own median (p95 reads a 1.5px rule in a 920x20 band as ABSENT at 2.9 dE while p99 finds it at 58.7), and the page side is read at full resolution with an integer stride rather than through a smoothing resize, which would cost a thin mark 40 percent of its spread and put a visible motif within a point of the survival floor.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post it today if the morning allows. Tuesday through Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time, is the strongest window, and the caption says seven days left, which is only true on August 25th. If it slips to Wednesday, the caption's count line has to move with it.
  • Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, before the first reader lands. It carries the caveat that the ordinance text was not publicly reachable, and that caveat should never arrive after a reader has already asked.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. That window decides how far the deck travels, and this topic will pull both police supporters and privacy readers.
  • If a commenter says the crime center already runs facial recognition, correct it with the chief's own words. The AI in the system today reads plates, the department says it does not use facial recognition, and the chief says it is unknown whether object recognition data can move through the system at all.
  • If someone asks for the ordinance's exact wording, say plainly that the text was not public when this was built and that slide 06 quotes the co-sponsor's description. Do not paraphrase it into something firmer.
  • Watch the Assembly agenda for September 1st once it posts. A postponement, an amendment or an AO number is the follow up post, and it is also the docket update.
  • Note saves and comments at 48 hours. This is the first deck built on a countdown structure with a cold number opener, so the number matters to the caption ledger.

SITE AND DATA CHECKS

GAS WATCH: PASS, read 2026-08-25, 7.25 Bcf, 55.8 percent of design, chart present. The reading is the cron's, not this run's. ledger/gaswatch.jsonl came out byte-identical to main's through the merge, which is the check that matters, because CINGSA keeps no archive to rebuild a corrupted series from.

SITE FIXES, two, both reader-facing. The docket's gold button read COMMENT NOW · CLOSES SEP 1 on the new Anchorage crime-center item, whose open room is a public hearing where a person speaks, not a written comment window. The verb was a constant hardcoded in two files; it is now data on the item from a closed set, rendered through one implementation. And the house-voice gate was failing the whole build on the ADN's own URL slug for an op-ed titled "public safety cannot come at the expense of civil liberties", a string this repo cannot rewrite without breaking the citation. A URL is now read as an address rather than as prose, in both the build gate and the daily sign-off, and both still fire on real prose.

ONE SUBSCRIBER EMAIL WENT OUT. docket_alerts sent "2 Alaska AI decisions land in the next few days", covering the ANA AI3 deadline on August 27th and this ordinance's September 1st hearing. That is the documented Phase 11 behaviour and the no-repeat ledger recorded both so they cannot resend, but it is outward-facing and it already happened.
